newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 100 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 100 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 70 billion bolivar ($145 million) auction of 177-day VE6MTMA=RR "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 17.48 percent coupon.

The bank said it would also offer 15 billion bolivars ($31 million) in 266-day bills VE9MTMA=RR with a 17.85 percent coupon, and another 15 billion bolivars of 358-day bills VE1YTMA=RR with a 18.24 percent coupon.
Some 30 billion bolivars of TEMs are due to mature on Thursday.

Coupons at the Wednesday auction are down from last week's 60 billion bolivar issue. Then 177-, 266- and 358-day notes carried 18.70, 19.13, and 19.58 percent coupons respectively for effective yields that fell, mostly at the short end of the curve, to 17.48, 20.48 and 21.19 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
